question: In the fluidized-bed co-incineration of sewage sludge, by what factor does the Fe content (wt %) of the agglomerate neck exceed that of the silica sand?
rendered:
The document "Bed Particle Layer Formation and Characteristics of Ilmenite Bed Particles Utilized in Fluidized Bed Combustion of Chicken Litter" does not provide information on the fluidized-bed co-incineration of sewage sludge.

The document "Co-Incineration of Real Municipal Sewage Sludge in a Fluidized Bed: Effects of the Coexistence of P, Fe, and Na on Agglomeration and Heavy Metal Emissions" provides the relevant information.

Table 3 presents the EDS analysis results for the primary elements on the silica sand surface and within the neck structure. The proportions of P and Fe are significantly higher than those in the silica sand.

EDS elemental distribution shows that Na is abundant in the neck structures, whereas the proportions of P and Fe are significantly higher than those in the silica sand.

Silica sand: 
- 97.5 at.% O, 
- 1.9 at.% Na, 
- 0.5 at.% the results shown 

Agglomerate:
- 32.6 at.% P, 
- 58.7 at.% O, 
- 2.7 at.% Fe, 
- 2.7 at.% Na, 
- 1.98 at.% the results shown 

The Fe content (wt %) of the agglomerate neck exceeds that of the silica sand by a factor of: 
(2.7/1.9) ≈ 1.42
